answer: A replica is proven not by a hash alone but by how fast it can be served: the registry measures round-trip time from a random vantage point and rejects answers slower than the bound for local storage. A ridge of delay exposes a provider fetching data from elsewhere instead of holding it. The spiral of the measurement is signed by the challenger, and the island of latency samples over an epoch builds a profile no remote-fetching Sybil can fake cheaply.
